audit_findings.title: The 2031-note financing state is not synchronized across numerator, denominator, and bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.150 billion note principal, equal to 18.6% of the $6.168 billion base equity value; 10.811495 million conversion shares, equal to 4.1% of the 262.633967 million denominator; removing only those shares computes to approximately $1.00 more per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: The financing state affects the diluted share denominator, interest retained in owner earnings, and treatment of note proceeds and principal in the cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Dilutive potential common shares include outstanding stock options, PSUs and RSUs.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated: the valuation includes all conversion shares even though the filing says the notes produced no potentially dilutive shares at the prevailing conversion state, while FY2025 owner earnings predates issuance and the bridge treats the note as outstanding debt without deducting principal. The share-only error understates value, but the treatment of debt-funded cash may overstate it, so the net direction is mixed. The $1.150 billion principal is large enough to make the unresolved state material.
audit_findings.action: Rerun two internally consistent cases using the filed conversion terms and capped calls: debt outstanding with no conversion shares and the effective interest burden retained, and as-converted with conversion shares, note principal, interest, and capped-call effects treated consistently.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may include customer-funded cash that is not surplus equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: $393.0 million of June 2026 contract liabilities, equal to 15.6% of $2.512162 billion cash and short-term investments and 6.4% of the $6.168 billion base equity value; full exclusion would equal approximately $1.50 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer-funded cash enters the bridge as cash and short-term investments, while the associated performance obligation affects future revenue, costs, and owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Contract liabilities were $ 390.8 million and $ 95.6 million as of December 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The contract liability is demonstrated, but the portion of June cash that is restricted economically or required to satisfy customer obligations is unresolved. Treating all cash as surplus while forecasting earnings from the funded services can double count value. The filed liability is sufficiently large relative to the cash bridge and base equity value to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each June 2026 customer advance to cash received, contract-liability classification, standby letters of credit, restrictions, expected service costs, and forecast revenue; rerun the bridge excluding the portion that is not surplus to operations.

audit_findings.title: The forecast may ignore the imminent Arizona capital-consumption cycle
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $2.5-$3.0 billion, equal to 9.6-11.5 times the $260.2 million owner-earnings anchor; first-half 2026 free cash flow was negative $269.860 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Required capital spending reduces near-term owner earnings and distributable cash; the resulting capacity, subsidies, and customer funding may affect subsequent growth and terminal economics.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect that our 2026 capital expenditures will be approximately $2.5 billion to $3.0 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The capital-consumption cycle is demonstrated, although its division between maintenance and value-creating growth investment is unresolved. Mechanically growing FY2025 owner earnings without explicitly timing this program can substantially overstate near-term cash available to owners. The disclosed spending is many times the anchor and is therefore material even before considering execution, utilization, or clawback risk.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $2.5-$3.0 billion program into maintenance, committed, and discretionary growth capital; map payment timing, the $1.4652 billion purchase obligations, customer contributions, tax credits, grants, and clawbacks; then rerun explicit-period owner earnings and resulting growth benefits.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease equipment costs may fall between the capex and debt rules
audit_findings.magnitude: $89.942 million of 2025 finance-lease principal payments and $59.860 million of 2025 noncash finance-lease right-of-use additions, respectively 34.6% and 23.0% of the $260.2 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Leased-equipment acquisition or replacement cost should reduce owner earnings exactly once, either through capital expenditure or an economically equivalent lease-cost adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our total remaining operating lease obligations and finance lease obligations were $82.9 million and $170.8 million, respectively, with $26.3 million and $51.8 million payable within 12 months, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed lease amounts are demonstrated, but their treatment in the owner-earnings calculation is not supplied. If cash property purchases exclude leased equipment while financing principal is also excluded, owner earnings omits a significant operating-asset cost. The potentially omitted amounts are large relative to the anchor, making the issue material; they must not both be deducted for the same equipment.
audit_findings.action: Trace finance-lease additions, amortization, interest, principal payments, purchases of formerly leased assets, and any amounts already included in maintenance capital; rerun owner earnings after capturing replacement economics exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The FY2025 anchor may retain a nonrecurring insolvency receipt
audit_findings.magnitude: $32.4 million pre-tax; $23.911 million after subtracting the filed $8.489 million tax effect, equal to 9.2% of the $260.2 million anchor and approximately $1.28 per base-case share if retained and capitalized under the same forecast path
audit_findings.mechanism: The receipt reduced FY2025 SG&A and therefore increases the net-of-tax owner-earnings anchor unless specifically removed before forecasting.
audit_findings.evidence: The net amount recognized from the Nanium Insolvency Receipt was $32.4 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The receipt's nonrecurring nature and reported amount are demonstrated; whether the valuation removed it is unresolved because no one-off reconciliation is supplied. Capitalizing a possible 9.2% after-tax anchor uplift through the explicit and terminal periods is material.
audit_findings.action: Produce the FY2025 owner-earnings reconciliation showing the Nanium receipt and its tax effect separately; remove any retained amount and rerun all scenarios, while separately reconciling machinery-sale gains and recurring disposal proceeds.

audit_findings.title: The anchor tax burden may not persist through the terminal period
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; filed reference amounts include a $3.1 million 2025 conditional-rate benefit, a $12.8 million valuation-allowance reversal, a 15.4% FY2025 effective tax rate, and a computed 13.6% effective rate for the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher normalized cash tax burden would reduce net owner earnings during the explicit forecast and terminal period.
audit_findings.evidence: As those conditional reduced tax rates expire, we expect that our tax expense will increase as income from those jurisdictions becomes subject to higher statutory income tax rates, thereby reducing our liquidity and cash flow.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporary incentives and their future expiration are demonstrated, and the low current tax burden is already embedded in the net-of-tax anchor. The disclosed $3.1 million conditional-rate benefit alone is only 1.2% of the anchor, but that does not bound the combined future effect of incentive expiration, jurisdictional earnings mix, Pillar Two taxes, valuation-allowance items, and offshore cash taxes. The record therefore cannot establish total materiality.
audit_findings.action: Build a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction cash-tax schedule through and beyond Singapore's 2028 incentive expiration, separate recurring taxes from discrete benefits, incorporate Pillar Two and remittance taxes, and rerun owner earnings and terminal value using the resulting normalized rates.
